A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3D-properties study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original toy-model simulations and Baichuan2 experiments on mathematical reasoning, poem/slogan generation, and preference discrimination.

after.justification: v2 retains original Baichuan2 experimental results and reports revised toy-model trajectories.

M1.justification: The Flex-DPO objective with separate chosen/rejected weights and the SFT-loss regularizer remain unchanged in Appendix B.2. SimPO is newly analyzed as an existing method; it is not introduced as a new proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The mathematical, poem/slogan, and four toy-scenario coverage is retained. However, v1 describes a heterogeneous COMMON training corpus, whereas v2 names HH-rlhf and UltraFeedback while retaining a COMMON reference. The PDFs do not establish whether UltraFeedback represents newly used data or newly disclosed constituents of the earlier mixture.

E2.justification: IPO and SLiC disappear from the reported toy-model comparisons when v1 Figures 5–8 are removed, although both remain in the mathematical comparison. The other empirical comparators are retained. SimPO receives theoretical analysis but no reported experimental comparison.

E3.justification: The Flex-DPO mathematical-results caption changes the rejected-response weight from 0.01 to 0.08 (v1 Table 10; v2 Table 9). Appendix D.1 adds a learning rate of 5e-6 while retaining 5e-7. The corpus table replaces 400,000 COMMON samples with source counts of 170,000 and 336,820. These are reported setting revisions with unresolved inconsistencies, not evidence that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Removing v1 Figures 5–8 eliminates the controlled IPO/SLiC analyses of likelihood stability across four on/off-policy conditions and their gradient diagnostics. This substantially reduces evidence about whether alternative objectives mitigate the three properties. The vanilla-DPO scenario analyses are revised, while poem-weight sensitivity and LLM convergence analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The minimum/maximum likelihood curves summarize responses rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: Figures 2–3 show substantially revised toy trajectories: the all-on-policy chosen-likelihood peak changes from approximately 0.58 to 0.41, while v2's off-chosen/on-rejected case peaks around 0.67. IPO/SLiC toy results are removed. LLM outcome tables retain their numerical values. The PDFs do not establish identical conditions underlying the revised toy results.

T1.justification: New Appendix B.3.3 derives SimPO gradients and their ratio, then introduces and proves Lemma 1 distinguishing limiting behavior according to beta versus rejected-response length. This substantially extends the formal analysis. Corollary 1 also corrects the DPO gradient ratio from positive to negative.

C1.justification: The three properties, regularization proposals, and data-distribution contributions remain central. However, the introduction strengthens the causal attribution of PPO's superiority: avoiding the properties changes from something that 'may in part' explain its advantage to something from which it 'stem largely'.

C2.justification: v2 explains coupled likelihood decline through shared tokens/patterns and adds a toy-to-token analogy. It replaces the specific untested token-level-DPO limitation with broader applicability caveats. It also interprets Flex-DPO as consistently outperforming alternatives, although retained Table 9 gives SLiC 38.7% versus Flex-DPO 38.0% on MATH's 4&5-point metric.

D1.justification: v2 newly details toy mini-batch pairing, explicitly references supplementary toy code, and specifies reference solutions in GPT-4 selection/evaluation. It revises the stated architectural basis of Baichuan2-33B from 7B to 13B and supplies named corpus counts. Most optimizer, batch-size, hardware, and supplementary-material disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Section 2.2 explicitly contrasts the work's optimization-dynamics analysis with Feng, Xu, and Tang's studies. References are added for SimPO, UltraFeedback, Best-of-N alignment, and an alignment survey; the token-level optimization reference by Zhong et al. is removed. The overall research positioning remains a diagnosis of DPO.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, toy-model explanation, and experimental narrative undergo extensive rewriting. The PPO analysis becomes Section 3.4, experiments are reorganized into separate regularization, RM-training, and PPO-comparison sections, and limitations move to Appendix D.3. Terminology changes include 'LLM unlearning' to 'response suppression'.

P2.justification: v2 replots Figures 2–3, corrects the ordering of the mixed-scenario displays, and removes four IPO/SLiC figures. It merges the model-specific mathematical tables, relocates the log-probability table and poem-sensitivity plot, and redisplays RM comparisons across the main text and appendix. Captions and conference formatting are extensively revised.

improvement.justification: The SimPO proof and clearer explanations add value, but v2 removes controlled IPO/SLiC evidence and introduces unresolved reporting problems. Appendix D.1 gives conflicting learning rates, and the Flex-DPO caption changes its parameter without changing scores. The revised all-on-policy toy peak is about 0.41, yet the text retains the earlier approximately 0.6 description. These substantive benefits and harms prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
